- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.8) but price declines, model may overreact; apply downward bias of 1–3% to offset sentiment-driven overconfidence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day rolling average as anchor for correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp drop (first 5–7 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive negative sentiment), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for risk-adjusted downside.
